Stages of link_encounters()

Source: R/utils-link-stages.R
check_inpatient_admission_data.Rd

Internal helpers that link_encounters() runs in order. Each takes the data produced by the previous stage and returns the next, so the exported function reads as a short pipeline and each stage can be understood and tested on its own.

Usage

check_inpatient_admission_data(
  inpatient_admission_data,
  is_missing,
  call = rlang::caller_env()
)

detect_patient_class_source(ed_data)

validate_has_been_flags(ed_data, verbose, call = rlang::caller_env())

split_patient_class_list(pc_list)

pair_mdt_timestamps(ed_data, pc_split_list, use_mdt, mdt_col_str)

long_from_patient_class_list(
  ed_data,
  pc_list_str,
  use_mdt,
  mdt_col_str,
  verbose
)

long_from_has_been_flags(ed_data, exclude_from_pivot, verbose)

bind_direct_admits(
  ed_long,
  inpatient_admission_data,
  verbose,
  key_cols = character(0),
  text_cols = character(0),
  call = rlang::caller_env()
)

as_text_cols(data, cols)

check_linking_columns(
  inpatient_admission_data,
  key_cols,
  call = rlang::caller_env()
)

add_class_time(ed_long)

build_episode_ids(
  ed_long,
  fac_col_str,
  visit_col_str,
  has_fallback,
  fallback_col_str,
  verbose
)

add_episode_metadata(ed_long, episode_id_vec)

collapse_episodes(result, merge_fields, merge_delimiter)

Arguments

inpatient_admission_data

A data frame of inpatient admissions. For bind_direct_admits(), the raw (not yet normalized) data frame.

is_missing

Logical. Whether inpatient_admission_data was omitted from the call.

call

The environment errors are attributed to; see resolve_col().

ed_data

The normalized ED data frame (clean_names_safe() already applied).

verbose

Logical. Whether to emit informational messages.

pc_list

A vector of C_Patient_Class_List values.

pc_split_list

The list returned by split_patient_class_list(): one character vector of patient classes per row of ed_data.

use_mdt

Logical. Whether C_Patient_Class_MDT_Updates is usable.

mdt_col_str

Name of the C_Patient_Class_MDT_Updates column, or NA_character_.

pc_list_str

Name of the C_Patient_Class_List column.

exclude_from_pivot

Character vector of HasBeen_ columns to leave out of the pivot.

ed_long

The long-format data frame (one row per patient class) built so far.

key_cols

Character vector of the linking columns (facility, visit, and the fallback column if any) that must exist in inpatient_admission_data. Defaults to none.

text_cols

Character vector of the linking identifier columns (facility_col, visit_col, and fallback_visit_col) to hold as text. Defaults to none.

data

A data frame. For as_text_cols(), one of the two pulls.

cols

Character vector of column names in data.

fac_col_str, visit_col_str

Names of the facility and visit columns in ed_long.

has_fallback

Logical. Whether fallback_visit_col was supplied.

fallback_col_str

Name of the fallback_visit_col column, or NULL.

episode_id_vec

Character vector of .episode_id values, one per row of ed_long.

result

The long-format data frame with episode metadata.

merge_fields

Named character vector of merge strategies, with snake_case names.

merge_delimiter

Delimiter used by the delimited merge strategies.

Value

check_inpatient_admission_data() returns its input invisibly or aborts. detect_patient_class_source() returns a list with use_pc_list, pc_list_str, use_mdt, and mdt_col_str. validate_has_been_flags() returns the HasBeen_ columns to exclude from the pivot. The remaining stages return the updated long-format data frame, except build_episode_ids(), which returns a character vector. check_linking_columns() returns NULL invisibly or aborts. as_text_cols() returns data with those columns as character.

Details

The stages, in the order link_encounters() calls them:

  1. check_inpatient_admission_data() aborts unless a data frame was supplied for inpatient_admission_data (there is no single-pull mode).

  2. detect_patient_class_source() finds the optional C_Patient_Class_List and C_Patient_Class_MDT_Updates columns, which decide how patient classes are derived.

  3. validate_has_been_flags() (only without C_Patient_Class_List) checks that the HasBeen_ flags needed to derive patient classes are present and reports which admission flag will be used.

  4. long_from_patient_class_list() or long_from_has_been_flags() reshapes ed_data to one row per patient class. long_from_patient_class_list() uses split_patient_class_list() to split each C_Patient_Class_List value into its classes and pair_mdt_timestamps() to attach C_Patient_Class_MDT_Updates timestamps to them.

  5. bind_direct_admits() tags inpatient_admission_data as "Direct Admit" and appends it, after check_linking_columns() has confirmed the linking columns exist in it and as_text_cols() has converted the linking identifier columns to text.

  6. add_class_time() fills the .class_time ordering column.

  7. build_episode_ids() builds the .episode_id for every row.

  8. add_episode_metadata() adds .episode_id, .patient_class_sequence, .episode_n_rows, and .index_encounter (TRUE on the one row per episode that the collapsed output keeps).

  9. collapse_episodes() reduces each episode to one row (return_format = "collapsed" only).

long_from_has_been_flags() pivots the HasBeen_ flags to long format. It preserves a copy of each pivoted column under an _orig name first, since pivot_longer() consumes the columns it pivots on. Every synthetic row produced from one original record describes that same record, so each should keep that record's true has_been_* values regardless of which flag triggered its own creation: an "Admitted->ED" escalation splits one row (HasBeenE = 1, HasBeenAdmitted = 1) into two synthetic rows (ED and Admitted), and both must still show has_been_e = 1 and has_been_admitted = 1. Without this, has_been_* end up NA (or, worse, silently wrong after cross-pull max() reconciliation) for any row that never came from inpatient_admission_data directly. HasBeenI, when excluded to prefer HasBeenAdmitted, is deliberately left out of the pivot rather than dropped from the data, so its true 0/1 value survives on every row.

build_episode_ids() treats a missing facility_col or visit_col value as an unknown identity, not as a match for every other missing value (see na_safe_group_id()), so only NA-key rows get a unique .episode_id and every other row keeps the normal "{facility}_{visit}" format. fallback_visit_col is the one deliberate exception: a row missing visit_col can still be confirmed to match another row via a secondary identifier. The three candidate id strings are built as plain vectors, not inside a dplyr verb, so the fallback lookup is never attempted when no fallback_visit_col was supplied.

add_episode_metadata() computes its columns over whole vectors keyed by episode (episode_class_sequence(), episode_primary_row()), not per episode inside dplyr's .by =: most episodes have a single row, and a per-episode R call for each of them dominated the run time.

collapse_episodes() deliberately avoids a per-episode helper applied through dplyr::group_modify(): that slices out a full-width single-row data frame per episode and binds all of them back together, which is the source of the memory and time blowup on a full year of data. It reconciles only the columns that change (has_been_* flags and merge_fields) as vectorized, per-episode-grouped column operations on the multi-row episodes, then keeps one row per episode.
